observations: Rain makes a steady sound against a closed window. A blue thread lies across an unfinished drawing on the table.
The rain stops. Water continues to fall from the roof at irregular intervals. The drawing has not moved.
A bell sounds twice in another room. One mark near the edge of the drawing could be an arrow or a fold in the paper.
A strip of afternoon light crosses the table. The blue thread is now in shadow, while the ambiguous mark is easier to see.
The window opens slightly. The paper lifts at one corner and settles. The mark remains visible after the corner falls flat.
The bell sounds once. A second sheet is placed beside the first; it contains a similar mark pointing in a different direction.
Outside, footsteps pass and fade. Both sheets remain on the table. Their marks resemble one another without being identical.
A small weight is placed on the first sheet. The blue thread passes beneath it. The window remains slightly open.
Rain returns, softer than before. The reflected window frame makes a line across the second sheet that was not drawn on it.
The light shifts and the reflected line disappears. The two original marks remain. No one has added an explanation.
The second sheet is turned over. Its reverse is blank. The first drawing and the blue thread remain where they were.
The room grows quieter. The rain can still be heard through the opening. The unfinished drawing is available to look at again.

What ordinary passages, absences, or counterexamples complicate the initial reading?
